crisis.excerpt: At this time terrible calamities began to lay waste the land. Ten suns appeared in the sky, the heat of which burnt up all the crops; dreadful storms uprooted trees and overturned houses; floods overspread the country. Near the Tung-t'ing Lake a serpent, a thousand feet long, devoured human beings, and wild boars of enormous size did great damage in the eastern part of the kingdom. Yao ordered Shen I to go and slay the devils and monsters who were causing all this mischief, placing three hundred men at his service for that purpose.
crisis.note: Quotation from E. T. C. Werner's 1922 English synthesis; it is not a direct translation of the ancient source it discusses.

suns.excerpt: After this first victory Shen I led his troops to the banks of the Hsi Ho, West River, at Lin Shan. Here he discovered that on three neighbouring peaks nine extraordinary birds were blowing out fire and thus forming nine new suns in the sky. Shen I shot nine arrows in succession, pierced the birds, and immediately the nine false suns resolved themselves into red clouds and melted away. Shen I and his soldiers found the nine arrows stuck in nine red stones at the top of the mountain.
suns.note: Quotation from E. T. C. Werner's 1922 English synthesis; it is not a direct translation of the ancient source it discusses.

narrativeBlocks.title: A land in crisis
narrativeBlocks.body: Werner's synthesis describes ten suns, storms, floods, a giant serpent, and destructive boars. Yao sends Shen I and a force of three hundred men to confront the calamities.

narrativeBlocks.title: The nine false suns
narrativeBlocks.body: Quotation from the cited English edition (whitespace normalized): “After this first victory Shen I led his troops to the banks of the Hsi Ho, West River, at Lin Shan. Here he discovered that on three neighbouring peaks nine extraordinary birds were blowing out fire and thus forming nine new suns in the sky. Shen I shot nine arrows in succession, pierced the birds, and immediately the nine false suns resolved themselves into red clouds and melted away. Shen I and his soldiers found the nine arrows stuck in nine red stones at the top of the mountain.”

narrativeBlocks.title: Arrows and red clouds
narrativeBlocks.body: In Werner's account, nine fiery birds create nine additional suns. Shen I shoots them; the false suns become red clouds and disappear.

narrativeBlocks.title: An early twentieth-century synthesis
narrativeBlocks.body: This episode is Werner's English retelling and arrangement of Chinese myth material. It should not be mistaken for one consistent version or a direct translation from a named early text.

narrativeBlocks.title: Cosmic crisis and skilled action
narrativeBlocks.body: The story joins environmental disaster with a hero's task, but its details belong to Werner's compiled version.
